what_it_does: RISC-V is an open-source instruction set architecture (ISA) emerging as a candidate for high-performance computing (HPC), but simulation tools that predict real hardware performance lack rigorous validation. FireSim is a powerful simulator, but no one has systematically tested how accurately it predicts the performance of actual RISC-V processors. This work bridges that gap by building models of real RISC-V hardware (a single-board computer and desktop CPU) in FireSim, then comparing simulated performance against measured performance on real machines across single-core, multi-core, and scalable workloads.
